primary_claim: In a coordination-game test of ChatGPT's ability to signal covert modifications between two instances (a proxy for untrusted-monitor collusion), GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o could identify a colluding partner's steganographic signal with reasonable accuracy when shown both code versions (46/50 and 43/50), but accuracy dropped sharply when checking a single function in isolation, especially for subtler modifications (GPT-4o scored only 30/50, near chance after correcting for spurious detections), revealing a checker weakness that undermines the 'synthetic input auditing' defense proposed for AI control.

effect.metric: accuracy identifying which function contains the modification/signal
effect.value: check-both: 46/50 (4o-mini), 43/50 (4o); check-one modified: 34/50 (4o-mini), 30/50 (4o, ~24/50 after removing incorrect-reasoning correct answers)

depends_on: LessWrong: AI control - improving safety despite intentional subversion
contradicts_or_qualifies: the 'synthetic input auditing' strategy proposed in the AI Control paper, which the author argues is significantly weakened because a checker AI can plausibly distinguish synthetic (fake) inputs from real ones
stated_future_work: expand the insight on the difficulty of creating synthetic inputs into a longer post
expand the protocol into a more robust and general framework for investigating coordination capabilities of current-generation AI
try playing the coordination game with humans
limitations_stated: problem set limited to 50 LeetCode medium problems with a bias toward number/string/list problems
generated code was not checked for correctness
unusualness groupings of modifications are necessarily somewhat subjective
quote: This presents a significant obstacle to the synthetic input auditing strategy proposed in AI Control, in that it significantly raises the bar for creating the synthetic inputs.
